source.title: Enhancing Neural Network Interpretability with Feature-Aligned Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Luke Marks; Alasdair Paren; David Krueger; Fazl Barez

record.tranche_reason: The study directly compares SAE decoder features with known synthetic input features, testing feature alignment with a different method from the original toy-model geometry experiments.
record.gate_note: The synthetic-data feature comparisons bear on V5. GPT-2 Small reconstruction and loss-recovered results, and EEG reconstruction results, evaluate SAE performance but do not measure the feature properties named by the claim versions. Cited results from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: Mainly a methods paper (MFR), but its motivating synthetic-data analysis compares baseline SAE decoder features with known ground-truth features. It shows baseline SAEs learn a seed-dependent cluster of features that match across SAEs but not the input. That bears on whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Authors conclude that cross-SAE feature similarity correlates with input-feature similarity on synthetic data, and that MFR recovers more input features. They report MFR improves reconstruction loss by up to 21.21% on GPT-2 Small layer-0 MLP outputs and 6.67% on EEG. GPT-2 reconstruction gains held only for the smaller k values (worse at k=24, 30), while loss recovered improved for all k.
record.recipe_differences: Trains sparse autoencoders with TopK sparsity, conditional weight reinitialization, and an auxiliary penalty encouraging decoder-feature similarity; it does not reproduce the original toy-network geometry method.
record.method_sensitivity: On GPT-2 Small, reconstruction-loss effects depended on TopK k relative to the other SAEs: the three smallest tested k values improved, while the two largest were equivalent or worse. Synthetic-data runs varied between larger and smaller inactive-feature clusters.
record.problems: The direct comparison with known input features is limited to synthetic data. The study does not establish feature completeness, stability, or canonical status for real neural-network representations. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the relevant feature-alignment results.
record.rows_left_out: GPT-2 Small and EEG reconstruction and loss-recovered results were left out because they do not measure the feature properties named by the claim versions. Figure-only SAE performance values were likewise not extracted.

untested.parts: No toy-network storage geometry, near-orthogonality, sparsity transition or phase structure; superposed synthetic data is only used as SAE input.
No neuron polysemanticity or importance-vs-capacity allocation.
No measure of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
GPT-2 Small results are reconstruction and loss-recovered only; no measure of feature spread across neurons or recovery of LLM features.
Completeness and canonicity in real models (GPT-2, EEG) not measured against any ground truth. Only synthetic Gaussian-feature data with TopK, tied-weight SAEs is tested.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: MMCS of baseline SAE decoder with the input feature matrix over training, inferior vs superior initialization (figure-only). Shows how much of F baseline SAEs recover and its initialization dependence.
Features in the non-input cluster were significantly less likely to be active after TopK (near-dead features).

record.verdict_notes: Primarily a methods paper; only the baseline synthetic analysis bears on V5. Rows r2 and r4 compare the authors' method with baselines and are delinked. No uncertainty estimates are given, and the cluster sizes are approximate.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses synthetic sparse inputs with more features than dimensions, but does not test toy-network storage geometry, near-orthogonality, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometric phases.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared capacity.
Does not measure polysemantic neurons arising without capacity pressure.
GPT-2 Small SAE reconstruction is evaluated, but the study does not measure whether features spread across neurons or whether sparse LLM features are recovered by a dictionary.
Tests alignment between SAE features and known features on synthetic data, not whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units for real neural-network representations.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional feature representations.

rows.subject: two baseline SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Compared pairwise feature similarity across SAE decoders with similarity to the synthetic input feature matrix
rows.measure: Correlation between feature similarity across SAEs and feature similarity with input features
rows.note: The positive association measures input alignment, but by itself does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.
rows.check: Correlation 0.625 between cross-SAE similarity and input-feature similarity: cross-run agreement tracks input correspondence only imperfectly, weakened by a non-input cluster. Partial rather than cannot_determine.

rows.subject: baseline SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Examined decoder-feature similarity across SAEs and similarity to the known input feature matrix
rows.measure: Size of cluster with high similarity across SAEs but low similarity to input features
rows.value: The larger cluster was approximately 15 features per SAE; a smaller-cluster outcome was approximately 5 features per SAE.
rows.note: The authors state that this cluster comprises features uncorrelated with the input feature matrix. The two approximate cluster sizes describe variation across runs, not a reported mean.
rows.check: State fine. Baseline SAEs (hidden size 512, 512 true features) learn a cluster of ~15 or ~5 features per SAE, varying with initialization, that are similar across SAEs but match no input feature. Counts are approximate and not out of 512 explicitly.

relationships.condition: Baseline TopK SAEs (hidden 512) on synthetic data, 512 features in 256 dims
relationships.reason: r1: cross-SAE agreement correlates only 0.625 with input match. r3: a seed-dependent cluster (~15 or ~5 features) is shared across SAEs yet matches no input feature. So SAE features are incomplete, and their stability does not ensure canonicity.
relationships.display_finding: Cross-SAE agreement correlated only 0.625 with matching an input feature, and a seed-dependent cluster of about 15 or 5 features was shared across SAEs yet matched no input feature.

tranche.reason: The synthetic ground-truth comparison identifies shared SAE features uncorrelated with input features, qualifying V5 despite the paper's primary methods contribution.

source_check.notes: Initialization differences are the authors' hypothesis for cluster-size variation, not an established causal result. Synthetic ground truth supports the qualification; these rows do not directly establish failures of canonicality in real-model activations.
